question: For the fixed X(8) isotropic Klein cover, which Aut(E_i)-orbit contains each selected nonzero two-torsion point x_i in the Borowka-Ortega isotropic Prym addition kernel: the unique Gaussian-CM-fixed point or one of the two points exchanged by multiplication by i?

parent_05aa.exact_use: All three invariant-side Q602 residues act on A[2] as nontrivial rank-one transvections. Prym-side compatibility reduces to the CM orbit of the selected x_i.

parent_05y.exact_use: X(8) has model u^2=xy, v^2=x^2-y^2, w^2=x^2+y^2; H is the even-sign V4; the three nontrivial H-character Prym elliptic factors are the three single-sign quotients and all are j=1728 with End=Z[i].

borowka_ortega.title: Klein coverings of genus 2 curves
borowka_ortega.journal: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 373 (2020), 1885-1907
borowka_ortega.exact_use: For the non-hyperelliptic genus-three quotient C_j, the three elliptic subvarieties E_sigma,E_tau,E_sigmat share a distinguished nonzero alpha in their intersection; the addition isogeny to J(C_j) has degree 8 and pullback polarization twice product-principal. For the isotropic Prym, E_{j sigma}=E_sigma/<alpha> etc., and the induced addition kernel is {(0,0,0),(x1,x2,x3)} with every x_i nonzero. The period model marks x_i=z_i/2.

sign_group_adapter.j_reason: A projective fixed point of the triple sign would require either u=v=w=0 or x=y=0; the three defining quadrics then force all coordinates zero.
sign_group_adapter.hyperelliptic_lift_reason: The full sign group modulo H has order two and quotienting C by all signs leaves the [x:y] line. Hence the odd-sign coset induces the hyperelliptic involution of C/H; choosing its fixed-point-free representative gives j.

selected_point_dual_kernel_identificatio.notation: q_i:E_i -> E_i_prime=E_i/<alpha>, where E_i_prime is E_{j sigma}, E_{j tau}, or E_{j sigma tau}
selected_point_dual_kernel_identificatio.original_addition_kernel: K0=ker(E_sigma x E_tau x E_sigma_tau -> J(C_j))
selected_point_dual_kernel_identificatio.K0_two_torsion_reason: Proposition 2.16 gives pullback of the principal polarization equal to twice the product principal polarization, so the polarized-isogeny kernel lies in the product 2-torsion.
selected_point_dual_kernel_identificatio.lift_argument: For x in ker(E'_1 x E'_2 x E'_3 -> J(C_j)/<alpha>), choose coordinate lifts a_i. Their sum lies in <alpha>; adding alpha to one coordinate does not change x and makes the lifted sum zero. Thus x lifts to K0 and every coordinate x_i belongs to q_i(E_i[2]).
selected_point_dual_kernel_identificatio.nonzero_coordinate_input: Lemma 4.13 proves every selected x_i is nonzero.
selected_point_dual_kernel_identificatio.unique_image: Since ker(q_i)=<alpha> has order two, q_i(E_i[2]) has order two. Therefore x_i is its unique nonzero point.
selected_point_dual_kernel_identificatio.dual_isogeny_consequence: For the degree-two isogeny q_i, ker(q_i^dual)=q_i(E_i[2]); hence E_i_prime/<x_i> is isomorphic to E_i.

gaussian_two_torsion_orbit_test.quotient_by_swapped_kernel: After translating (1,0) to the origin, the 2-isogenous quotient is y^2=x^3-6x^2+x, j=287496; the (-1,0) case is isomorphic.
gaussian_two_torsion_orbit_test.criterion: On a j=1728 elliptic curve, a nonzero order-two subgroup has j=1728 quotient iff it is the unique Gaussian-CM-stable subgroup.
gaussian_two_torsion_orbit_test.application: Each E_i_prime has j=1728 by 05Y and E_i_prime/<x_i>=E_i has j=1728 by the fixed X(8) quotient replay, so every selected x_i is CM-fixed.
